reason: Research was thin: three searches returned no dated coverage of the November 2026 energy, rates or equity moves, so this is a packet-plus-late-October-context decision and I am saying so plainly. The book is +3.61% with a dividend-aristocrat core (JNJ, PG, KO, MCD, ABT, MMM, MSFT, XLF) that is in the black, and 39.5% cash earning 4% APY. The XLE leg (12%, -4.30%) is the main drag, but the oil evidence I found was undated and mixed, so I have no confirmed reason to cut it at the 2026-11-09 close. The TLT short (5%, +0.34%) is the one leg that looks more exposed: an October 23 report said yields may have peaked, and a November 4 refunding was flagged as a possible bond-price turning point. That argues against adding to the short, but I could not confirm the refunding outcome, and a full rebalance costs real basis points on a $1,000 book. Holding is the better trade-off given the evidence.
